title: As A.I. Agents Begin Shopping, Brands Are Changing Their Sales Pitch
source_used: The New York Times, read via The Business Times (Singapore) syndication credited NYTIMES
key_facts: New startups (Limy, backed by Andreessen Horowitz; New Generation; Gauge) sell services that make brands' products legible to AI shopping agents rather than to human eyes.
Adobe: traffic to US retail sites from AI sources rose 393% in 2026.
Morgan Stanley research: agent-influenced spending could reach up to 20% of US e-commerce, about $385 billion, by 2030.
RTA Store, a family cabinetry retailer, paid New Generation $15,000 to restructure its site for agents and expects to spend up to $12,000 a month on agent visibility.
New Generation, with Visa, scores a website's readiness for agents from 1 to 100 by simulating agent visits.
Some stores, including Amazon, block some AI shopping agents.
Skeptics (Jacquard's Toby Coulthard, FTI's Akshat Trivedi) say models change faster than tactics and compare the rush to the early SEO boom.
quote_evidence: "When you advertise to humans, you target eyeballs, emotions and dopamine, but when you advertise to agents, you advertise to logic, a very mathematical logic," said Aviv Shamny, co-founder and CEO of Limy
Traffic to US retail sites from AI sources increased 393 per cent in 2026, according to a report from Adobe.
By 2030, "agent-influenced spend" might constitute up to 20 per cent of total US e-commerce, or US$385 billion, according to Morgan Stanley research.
why_it_matters_hint: Marketing money is starting to move toward persuading machines, not people, as Meta's and OpenAI's agents begin buying.
notes: NYT original blocked (403); the Business Times carries the NYT text with a NYTIMES credit, so NYT is the source. Trend piece, not a single event.
